provenance.instrument: City of Bradford Zoning Ordinance (Code Chapter 220 Zoning, Ord. No. 3231 of 6-23-2009, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 BR1254, City of Bradford, McKean County (220-8 'County': 'McKean County, Pennsylvania'). The code was adopted as a whole by Ord. No. 3296 of 5-14-2024. Each district article states its authorized uses and its area and bulk rules as web text. The zoning map and three appendix figures are PDF attachments and were not opened. Floodplain rules are Chapter 114 Floodplain Management
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 version shown: 'Code 2026-08-11'. New Laws lists no legislation awaiting codification (0)
checks: ADU: the code has no accessory dwelling unit term. A 'Guesthouse', defined as 'A small, separate house on the grounds of a larger one, used for accommodating guests' (220-8, added 3-26-2019 by Ord. No. 3231.2), is an accessory use by special exception in R-1, R-2 and R-3 (220-23B(2)(e), 220-31B(2)(e), 220-39B(2)(e)). Article XIII gives it no specific standards, so the general special exception standards of 220-89 apply. C-1 and C-2 list it as a principal use by special exception (220-55B(1)(j), 220-64B(1)(j)), but there it cannot be added beside a house (220-12D, 220-123C(3))
A guesthouse is read here as the code's detached ADU form, with the occupancy limit its definition sets. The code sets no size cap and no owner rule for it
Parking: 'Guesthouse: 1 space for each apartment in addition to 2 spaces required for the existing dwelling' (220-114C). Any fraction of a space counts as one (220-114A)

Accessory structures in C-D, R-1, R-2 and R-3: 'one story, but no more than 20 feet'. Accessory buildings and roofed projections may cover at most 30% of a required rear yard (40% on a corner lot) in R-1, R-2 and R-3 (220-94C(7)(b)). Detached garages and storage structures stay out of the required front yard, 5 ft from a side line, 3 ft from a rear line and 10 ft from the dwelling (220-94C(7)(a)). The code gives no accessory yards for a guesthouse, so the district yards are read as the safe figures. On a corner lot in R-1, R-2 and R-3 the side yard along the street has its own rule, starting at 10% of the lot width up to 10 ft (220-94A(4))

Uses: in C-D, R-1, R-2 and R-3 'any use not specifically listed as an authorized use in the zoning district shall not be permitted' (220-12B). M-C authorizes 'only the following uses', and they include no dwelling (220-47). In C-1, C-2, M-1 and M-2 a use not listed may be allowed as a comparable use by special exception if it is of the same general character as a listed use (220-12C, 220-90I). A single-family or two-family dwelling must be the only principal structure on its lot (220-12D), and an accessory structure may not be built until the principal structure exists on the lot (220-12G)

C-1 and C-2 list no single-family dwelling, so a house there is a nonconforming use. 'Where a nonconforming use exists on a lot, a conforming use shall not be established on the same lot unless the nonconforming use is discontinued' (220-123C(3)), and the house must stay the only principal structure (220-12D). So the guesthouse listing there does not reach a lot with a house. In C-1 each dwelling unit needs at least 400 sq ft as an efficiency, 550 sq ft with one bedroom and 750 sq ft with two (220-56H)

Conversion apartment: a unit created inside an existing single-family dwelling is a special exception in R-2 (one new unit) and R-3 (up to four), at least 400 sq ft each, with one added parking space. Detached garages and other accessory structures may not be converted to dwelling units under this listing (220-90J)
Two-family dwellings: a special exception in R-2 on a 10,000 sq ft site, 5,000 sq ft per unit (220-90CC), and permitted by right in R-3 on 4,000 sq ft (220-39, 220-40)
Lots of record: a lot of record may be built on with a use the district permits though it is below the area and width minimums, if it meets the yards, height and coverage (220-125A)

Floodplain (Chapter 114, FIRM of 12-22-2016): a permit for any construction or development. In a floodway no new construction or development without an engineering analysis of no rise and a DEP permit. In an AE area without a floodway nothing within 50 ft landward of the top of bank without a DEP permit (114-18B(2)(b)). New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure have the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation, the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft (114-23A, 114-38). An accessory structure that is not elevated may not be used for human habitation and may have at most 200 sq ft (114-23E). So an existing garage below that level cannot become a guesthouse, while a new guesthouse can be built elevated. 'No variances shall be granted for a proposed accessory structure that exceeds 600 square feet in size', and any such variance needs a signed nonconversion agreement (114-36C). No variance may allow any rise in a floodway, or a rise of more than one foot in an AE area without a floodway (114-36A, B)
Rooming houses are also a special exception in R-1, R-2, R-3, C-1 and C-2 (added 2019). They are not dwelling units for one household and are not read as an ADU path

Approvals: if land development approval is needed, the Chapter 191 application goes to the Planning Commission after the special exception (220-88A(4)). A special exception expires if no land development, grading, building or occupancy permit application is filed within 12 months, with one 12-month extension possible (220-88B)

Historic District Overlay: properties in the overlay on the zoning map are also subject to Chapter 125, Historic Preservation, with a Board of Historical Architectural Review and rules for altering structures (220-111). Chapter 125 asks for a certificate of appropriateness (125-8). Chapter 125 was not read in full
Steep slopes and stream buffers: the code has no steep slope rules, and the riparian buffer standards of Chapter 187 Article VI are reserved (187-18)

Read in full: 220-9 to 220-13, 220-14 to 220-62 (C-D, R-1, R-2, R-3, M-C and C-1 articles), 220-63 to 220-70 (C-2), 220-87 to 220-90W, 220-90CC, 220-112 to 220-115, 220-122 to 220-126, 114-23, and 220-8 from A to 'Lot area'. Read in part: 220-8 'Lot coverage' and later lot terms (screenshot), M-1 and M-2 use lists (in-page search only), 220-94 (screenshots), 220-131 to 220-133, 114-16 to 114-18. Not read: 220-0 to 220-7, the rest of 220-8, 220-73 to 220-78 and 220-81 to 220-86 (M-1 and M-2 area and bulk), 220-90X to BB except part of BB, 220-90DD, 220-91 to 220-93, 220-95 to 220-111, 220-116 to 220-121, 220-127 to 220-130, 220-134 to 220-149, Chapter 114 except the sections named, Chapter 191 (subdivision and land development) and the zoning map. Searched the code for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, extended family, household employee, elder cottage, tenant house, supplemental dwelling, temporary dwelling, apartment addition, living quarters, caretaker, conversion, care of, guest house, two-family and accessory building. Also read later: 220-91 to 220-103, 220-111, 220-127 to 220-139, 220-90X to 220-90DD, the M-1 area and bulk rules and Chapter 114 in full except 114-30 and 114-31. Not read: Chapter 125 (only search snippets of 125-8), Chapter 127 (only the 127-10 snippet) and Chapter 191. Open points: whether a guesthouse may ever be let as a home of its own (the code's words limit it to guests), whether Chapter 191 exempts a guesthouse beside a house from land development review, whether a guesthouse takes the garage yards of 220-94C(7) or the district's principal yards, and whether a guesthouse may be added over a garage.

term.note: 'A small, separate house on the grounds of a larger one, used for accommodating guests' [Added 3-26-2019 by Ord. No. 3231.2]. The code has no accessory dwelling unit term

status.note: A guesthouse is an accessory use by special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board in R-1, R-2 and R-3

scope_districts.note: Accessory use by special exception in R-1, R-2 and R-3. C-1 and C-2 list it as a principal use, which cannot be added beside a house (220-12D, 220-123C(3))

status_outside.note: M-1 and M-2 list no guesthouse and no dwelling. A use not listed there may be allowed as a comparable use by special exception (220-12C)

value.note: 'In the C-D, R-1, R-2 and R-3 Districts, any use not specifically listed as an authorized use in the zoning district shall not be permitted in that zoning district.' C-D does not list a guesthouse

C-1 and C-2 list a guesthouse as a principal use by special exception but list no single-family dwelling, so a house there is a nonconforming use. 'Where a nonconforming use exists on a lot, a conforming use shall not be established on the same lot unless the nonconforming use is discontinued', and the house must be the only principal structure on the lot (220-12D). So a guesthouse cannot be added beside a house there
'In the M-C Medical Center District, only the following uses are authorized', and the list names no dwelling and no guesthouse. M-C has no path for comparable uses (220-12C)

path.note: 'Guesthouse' under Uses by special exception, Accessory uses, in R-1, R-2 and R-3. The Zoning Hearing Board decides after a public hearing on the general standards of 220-89

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the hardship findings of 220-132A to E. No bar on a use variance

unlisted_use_path.note: Comparable uses not specifically listed, a special exception in C-1, C-2, M-1 and M-2. M-1 and M-2 list no dwelling, so a guesthouse there is not read as comparable. C-1 and C-2 list a guesthouse itself, which cannot be added beside a house. Two-family dwellings are listed in R-2 and R-3, where unlisted uses are barred

unlisted_use_scope.quote: Uses of the same general character as any of the uses authorized as permitted uses by right or uses by special exception in the zoning district in which the property is located

value.name: Conversion apartment (R-2, R-3)
value.conditions: A dwelling unit created inside an existing single-family dwelling, by special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board. Each unit at least 400 sq ft of gross floor area with its own living, sleeping, kitchen and sanitary facilities. In R-2 only one new unit in a single-family dwelling, in R-3 up to four. Detached garages and other accessory structures may not be converted to dwelling units. Safe ingress and egress and adequate turnaround areas for the residents' cars on the lot. One parking space for each apartment besides the 2 for the house

requires.condition: An existing single-family dwelling to adapt
At least 800 sq ft in the house, since the existing unit and the new one each need 400 sq ft of gross floor area

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-2)
value.conditions: A building with two dwelling units, by special exception. 'The minimum site required to develop two-family dwellings shall be 10,000 square feet' and 5,000 sq ft per dwelling unit. A two-family dwelling made inside an existing single-family dwelling meets the conversion apartment rules. Two parking spaces per unit
value.note: The single-family or two-family dwelling must be the only principal structure on the lot (220-12D), so a new two-family building takes the place of the house

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-3)
value.conditions: A building with two dwelling units is a permitted use. 4,000 sq ft and 40 ft wide, front 20 ft, side 4 ft, rear 20 ft or the building height, coverage 60%. Two parking spaces per unit
value.note: The single-family or two-family dwelling must be the only principal structure on the lot (220-12D). R-3 also lists the conversion apartment, a unit made inside an existing single-family dwelling, by special exception, and 220-90CC(4) sends a house made into two units to the conversion rules. So the stronger reading is that a new two-family building is by right and a second unit made inside the existing house is the special exception

value.name: Infill housing (R-1, R-2, R-3)
value.conditions: Newly built single-family or two-family dwellings, or townhouses of up to four units, on a lot where deteriorated dwelling units stood before they were demolished. A lot below the district minimum may be used if 75% of the yards can be met. Design compatible with the houses on the same block

requires.condition: Deteriorated dwelling units stood on the lot and were demolished

value.note: C-2 permits infill housing by right (220-64A(1)(zzz))

land_development_second_building.note: The zoning chapter defines land development to include 'A group of two or more residential or nonresidential buildings, whether proposed initially or cumulatively'. Chapter 191 was not read. It may leave out an accessory building added beside an existing house, as the state planning code does (MPC 107). Ask the zoning officer

building_types.note: The guesthouse stands 'on the grounds of a larger one'. The definition does not name a house type

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: The R districts give a lot area by dwelling type, not per unit, and say nothing of a guesthouse

districts_read_no_listing.note: M-C, M-1 and M-2 list no dwelling and no guesthouse

value.condition: In an identified floodplain area (Chapter 114) every construction or development needs a floodplain permit. In a floodway no new construction, substantial improvement or other development is allowed unless an engineering analysis shows no rise in flood levels, and no new construction or development without a DEP permit. In an AE area without a floodway the work, together with all other existing and anticipated development, may not raise flood levels more than one foot. New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure need the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation (the base flood elevation plus 1.5 ft). In an A zone without flood data the city may require the lowest floor at least 3 ft above the highest adjacent grade.

no_variance.quote: No variance shall be granted for any construction, development, use, or activity within any floodway area/district that would cause any increase in the BFE
no_variance.note: Nor in an AE area without a floodway for anything that, together with all other existing and anticipated development, would raise the base flood elevation more than one foot at any point

value.condition: In an AE area without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection Regional Office'.

In an identified floodplain area an accessory structure that is not elevated or floodproofed 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation', may have no sanitary facilities or fixed utility equipment and at most 200 sq ft of floor area. A larger one below the base flood elevation needs a variance and a recorded nonconversion agreement. No variance may be granted for one over 600 sq ft. So an existing garage below the regulatory flood elevation cannot become a guesthouse.

disputed_by.note: The rule is for accessory structures that are not elevated or floodproofed. A building raised so that its lowest floor is at or above the regulatory flood elevation, as 114-23A asks of a residential structure, may not be reached. Work of 50% or more of the building's market value must fully comply (114-34C)

no_variance.quote: No variances shall be granted for a proposed accessory structure that exceeds 600 square feet in size. A signed nonconversion agreement is required as a condition of receiving the variance
no_variance.note: Any such variance needs a signed nonconversion agreement, so the structure stays out of use as living space

value.condition: In an identified floodplain area a new guesthouse is a residential structure: its lowest floor, including any basement, must be at or above the regulatory flood elevation (the base flood elevation plus 1.5 ft). An accessory structure left below that level may not be used for human habitation.

In the Historic District Overlay shown on the zoning map, the property is also subject to Chapter 125, Historic Preservation. Altering a structure there needs a certificate of appropriateness from City Council after review by the Board of Historical Architectural Review.
An accessory structure may not be built until the principal structure it serves exists on the lot, and it stands on the same lot.

types_allowed.note: 'A small, separate house on the grounds of a larger one'. A new separate house, or an accessory building turned into one

types_not_addressed.note: The code does not say whether quarters above a garage are a separate house

max_sqft.note: The definition says 'small' and gives no number

max_height_ft.note: 'All accessory structures: one story, but no more than 20 feet'

setback_rear_alley_ft.note: The district rear yard (20 ft or the building height for principal structures) is read as the safe figure, alley or not. Detached garages and storage structures may stand 3 ft from a rear line (220-94C(7)(a))

separation_ft.note: Detached garages and storage structures stay 10 ft from the dwelling. The code sets no distance for a guesthouse

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: The district rows send accessory yards to 220-94C, which gives yards only for listed kinds of accessory structures such as detached garages and storage structures, not a guesthouse. The district's own yards are read as the safe figures

value.where: A detached garage or storage structure accessory to a dwelling, and a guesthouse made in one if those yards still hold: not in the required front yard, at least 10 ft from the dwelling and 5 ft from any other structure
In R-1, R-2 and R-3, accessory buildings and roofed projections

The housing code groups a guesthouse with hotels, inns and bed-and-breakfasts (127-10). The code does not allow it as a separate rental home in words. Ask the zoning officer before renting it.
